name: studio
description: Scrapshift Studio Director: every chat reports itself to docs/studio/sessions/<app-session-id>.json, a worker's commit that stages docs/studio/ is refused, /studio shows the board of every chat (pane, text and toasts), /director makes a fresh chat the Studio director (role, board snapshot on each prompt, notes, a guard against building), and auto model routes each subagent by full model id from docs/studio/model_policy.md (never the chat's own model or effort), and the director chat resets itself between turns (a mod-run /clear past 600k tokens or after 55 min away, once any decision is in its notes), and the board pane has an ask box: one-shot questions answered from the board by one tool-less model call, with no chat context. The pane is a dashboard: usage bars, tabs (board, kanban, notes, models, ask), a card per chat, and in the director chat buttons and a field that send prompts to the chat itself. Stage 8: the director recalls from a memory graph built from files (graphify's idea, our code): a <studio-recall> block on each prompt, tools to recall, connect, remember and read one section, a nudge before big docs, checks before it starts a chat, and a Haiku brain pass whose answers stay outside the repo. Stage 9: a Map tab draws the graph as a mind map around one node, with buttons that move its focus and what the director is reminded of beside it, and /studio map opens the full map (pan, zoom, fold, search) as a page written outside the repo. Stage 10: the Map tab opens on the plan, a mind map of the milestones and their stages coloured by state (waiting on you, building, to review, done, planned), with buttons to pick a stage and answer, brief or start it, a field to plan a new one, and a studio_plan tool for the director. Stage 11: the leads (docs/studio/leads.md): the board, the snapshot and /studio group chats under their lead (who started them, up the chain, or the lead that adopted them), a By lead | By state switch on the Board tab, a lead chat gets its own chats on each prompt, and the one-builder rule is gone from the role and the start checks.
